description: QoL #3 — Deep-linkable run/task URLs with the native History API (NO router). Pure URL parse/serialize module (viewHash) with unit + fast-check round-trip tests, kept SEPARATE from a useDeepLink hook that wires it to window.history pushState/replaceState + a popstate listener. Integrate into App.tsx (view state is React state, not a router) so on load the URL restores the view (open the run; if a taskId is present and the task exists, open its logs), navigation updates the URL without reload, and browser back/forward works. Unknown/invalid run or task falls back to fleet / run-with-no-task — never crash, never fabricate. Sequenced LAST because it wires App.tsx + FleetView + RunDetailView together.
steps: Create frontend/src/navigation/viewHash.ts: `export type ViewState = { kind: 'fleet' } | { kind: 'run'; runId: string; taskId?: string }`. `parseViewHash(hash: string): ViewState` for the ONE scheme '#/run/<runId>' and '#/run/<runId>/task/<taskId>' (URL-decode the id segments); any other input ('', '#', '#/', unknown paths, '#/run/' with empty id) -> { kind: 'fleet' }; MUST never throw. `serializeViewHash(state: ViewState): string` producing '#/' for fleet, '#/run/<encoded>' for a run, '#/run/<encoded>/task/<encoded>' for a run+task. Keep this file free of React/DOM.

Create frontend/src/navigation/viewHash.test.ts: unit cases ('#/run/r1' -> run r1; '#/run/r1/task/t1' -> run r1 task t1; ''/'#'/'#/'/'#/garbage'/'#/run/' -> fleet; ids with reserved chars round-trip). fast-check round-trip property: for runId and optional taskId drawn from non-empty strings, parseViewHash(serializeViewHash(state)) deep-equals state; serializeViewHash(parseViewHash(x)) is idempotent for valid hashes; parseViewHash never throws on an arbitrary string.

Create frontend/src/navigation/useDeepLink.ts: a hook that on mount parses window.location.hash via parseViewHash for the initial ViewState, subscribes to 'popstate' to re-parse on back/forward, and returns `{ state, navigate }` where navigate(next: ViewState, opts?: { replace?: boolean }) serializes via serializeViewHash and calls window.history.pushState/replaceState(null, '', hash) WITHOUT reloading. Guard against a missing window (defensive for the test/SSR env). Keep ALL parse/serialize logic in viewHash.ts (this file only does DOM/History wiring).

Create frontend/src/navigation/useDeepLink.test.ts: use @testing-library/react renderHook; seed window.location.hash, spy window.history.pushState/replaceState (vi.fn), dispatch a popstate event. Assert initial state parsed from the seeded hash; navigate({kind:'run',runId:'r1'}) pushes '#/run/r1'; navigate(..., {replace:true}) calls replaceState; a popstate with a changed hash updates the returned state. Restore hash + spies in afterEach.

Edit frontend/src/App.tsx: in Dashboard, use useDeepLink to drive navigation. On mount map the initial ViewState -> existing state: a 'run' state sets selectedRunId (and remembers an optional pendingTaskId handed to RunDetailView); 'fleet' leaves the list. In onSelectRun, goToFleet, and the run<->fleet transitions, call navigate(...) to sync the hash (push on user navigation). Subscribe to the hook's state so popstate updates selectedRunId. Keep showReports/compareRunIds OUT of the hash scheme (fleet/run/task only) and clear them on fleet/run navigation exactly as the existing handlers do. An invalid/unknown hash resolves to fleet (no crash, no fabrication).

Edit frontend/src/rundetail/RunDetailView.tsx: add optional props `initialTaskId?: string` and `onTaskSelectionChange?: (taskId: string | null) => void`. After tasks load (phase === 'ready'), if initialTaskId matches a task in `tasks`, set logsSelection to { kind:'TASK', taskId, label } ONCE (guard with a ref so live task updates don't re-trigger it); if it does not match, leave no selection (never crash/fabricate). Invoke onTaskSelectionChange(taskId|null) from the task-selection/clear paths so App can update the hash. App passes initialTaskId={pendingTaskId} and an onTaskSelectionChange that calls navigate for '#/run/<id>/task/<taskId>' or '#/run/<id>'.

Add/extend frontend/src/App.test.tsx (create if absent): render Dashboard (mock-mode renders directly) with injectable data stubs (via FleetView/RunDetailView props or a vi.mock of '../api/client'); seed location.hash='#/run/r1' and assert the run detail opens for r1; '#/run/r1/task/t1' opens that task's logs when the stub supplies task t1; an unknown hash shows the fleet; selecting a run updates window.location.hash (spy pushState) and back-to-fleet resets it. Extend RunDetailView.test.tsx to cover initialTaskId present (opens logs) and absent (ignored).

Final whole-task gate: confirm no router was added and no new dependency: `grep -r "react-router" frontend/src` returns nothing and `git diff --exit-code frontend/package.json frontend/package-lock.json` is clean.
acceptance_criteria: `npx vitest run src/navigation` passes, including the fast-check round-trip property (>=100 iterations) and the useDeepLink hook tests.
On load, '#/run/<id>' opens that run and '#/run/<id>/task/<taskId>' opens the task's logs when the task exists; an unknown/invalid run or task falls back to fleet / run-with-no-task without crashing.
Opening a run, selecting a task, and going back to fleet update window.location.hash via pushState/replaceState with no full reload; browser back/forward (popstate) restores the corresponding view.
parseViewHash never throws and never fabricates a run/task; the pure module has no React/DOM imports.
No react-router import exists under frontend/src and frontend/package.json / package-lock.json are unchanged; `npm run build` + `npm run lint` + `npm test` (full) succeed.

findings: Implemented QoL #3 deep links with the native History API, no router, no new deps. New files: src/navigation/viewHash.ts (pure parse/serialize, no React/DOM; one scheme '#/'/'#/run/<id>'/'#/run/<id>/task/<id>', URL-encoded id segments, never throws, never fabricates — malformed escape or empty id falls back to fleet, missing task id -> run with no task), src/navigation/viewHash.test.ts (unit + fast-check round-trip/idempotence/totality, 500 runs each), src/navigation/useDeepLink.ts (hook: initial parse of window.location.hash, popstate re-parse, navigate() via history.pushState/replaceState without reload, defensive against missing window), src/navigation/useDeepLink.test.ts (renderHook; seeded hash, spied push/replaceState, dispatched popstate). RunDetailView gained optional initialTaskId + onTaskSelectionChange props: a ref-guarded one-time restore after phase==='ready' opens the task's logs only if it exists (ignored otherwise, no crash/fabrication), and a selectedTaskId-driven notification effect reports taskId|null to the shell. App.tsx now calls useDeepLink; view state stays plain React state. Key implementation details worth remembering: (1) RunDetailView is now keyed by selectedRunId so navigating between runs (click or back/forward) remounts with fresh queries + fresh restore — the per-mount 'query once' guard otherwise blocked re-querying on a runId change. (2) The notification effect is suppressed until the one-time restore has run (restoredInitialTask ref) so it never pushes a premature null that would clobber the task segment the restore is about to consume. (3) App wraps navigate in navigateHash, which records the serialized hash key in lastAppliedHashRef BEFORE navigating, so the inbound reconcile effect ignores our own outbound navigations and only reacts to real popstate/initial changes (prevents it from tearing down the freshly-registered logs split-panel slot). (4) showReports/compareRunIds are kept OUT of the hash; any inbound/fleet/run navigation clears them. Tests: added App.test.tsx 'Dashboard deep links (#3)' describe (initial run hash opens run; run/task hash opens the task logs via the shell split-panel slot; unknown hash -> fleet; non-existent task -> run with no task; select pushes '#/run/<id>' and back pushes '#/'; popstate restores fleet) and two RunDetailView.test.tsx cases (initialTaskId present opens logs, absent/non-matching ignored). Test-infra notes for this suite: must NOT use vi.restoreAllMocks() in afterEach (it resets the module-level vi.mock('./api/client') fns to return undefined and a prior test's unmounted RunDetailView then resolves a dangling query with undefined tasks -> selectLayer crash) — restore only the specific history spies; and Cloudscape SplitPanel is mocked to a context-free pass-through in App.test.tsx because the real one throws 'can only be used inside app layout' under the pass-through AppLayout mock. Verification all green: npx vitest run src/navigation src/App.test.tsx src/rundetail/RunDetailView.test.tsx = 83 passed; grep react-router src = none; git diff package.json/package-lock.json = clean; npm run lint = 0 errors; npm run build = ok; full npm test = 424 passed across 43 files. node_modules was already present in the worktree (no npm install needed).
